teachingLessons.title: Disease causes and germ theory
teachingLessons.goal: Explain how evidence connects a pathogen to disease while avoiding the claim that all microbes are harmful.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Compare bacteria, viruses and other pathogens
teachingLessons.goal: Identify a cause, its route of spread and why a treatment that works on bacteria need not work on a virus.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Communicable disease and unequal risk
teachingLessons.goal: Compare communicable and non-communicable disease and explain how environment and access affect risk without blaming individuals.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Food safety and preservation
teachingLessons.goal: Trace how storage and food-handling conditions affect microbial growth and contamination.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Sanitation, sterilization and aseptic practice
teachingLessons.goal: Distinguish cleaning, disinfection, antisepsis and sterilization in an appropriate context.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Outbreaks, epidemics and historical impact
teachingLessons.goal: Use time, place and affected population to distinguish outbreak, epidemic and pandemic; discuss historical impacts with appropriate context.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Public systems for water, waste and air
teachingLessons.goal: Follow a public-health pathway from monitoring to treatment and explain why shared infrastructure changes exposure.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Guidelines, risk decisions and the Walkerton case
teachingLessons.goal: Evaluate the evidence behind a community health decision, separating factual timeline from ethical judgment.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Physical barriers and inflammation
teachingLessons.goal: Trace first- and second-line responses and explain swelling, redness and warmth without treating them as a diagnosis.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Antigens, antibodies and immune response
teachingLessons.goal: Sequence a simplified immune response and distinguish antigens from antibodies.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Blood compatibility, vaccines and immunity
teachingLessons.goal: Compare active/passive immunity and explain why blood compatibility and vaccines require more context than a single slogan.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Medicines, antibiotics and safe choices
teachingLessons.goal: Distinguish symptom relief from treatment of a bacterial infection and explain antibiotic resistance.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: DNA, chromosomes and inheritance
teachingLessons.goal: Connect genes, DNA and chromosomes; interpret source karyotypes without reducing all biological sex to one chromosome pair.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Genotypes and Punnett squares
teachingLessons.goal: Use a clearly stated single-gene model to calculate possibilities and its limits.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Read and construct pedigrees
teachingLessons.goal: Read the Q11 family pedigree, then use the separate Q12 pedigree to identify evidence for recessive inheritance in the intended simple model.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Mutations, mutagens and genetic disorders
teachingLessons.goal: Separate changes in DNA from exposure claims and interpret health examples with care.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

teachingLessons.title: Genetic research and ethical decisions
teachingLessons.goal: Compare benefits, limitations and stakeholder concerns using evidence and respectful language.
teachingLessons.disposition: Teach and practise online; retain exact original workbook question and its diagram/table as source work.

sourceDispositionRules: Source workbook diagrams, tables and question subparts are retained in the original PDF and get a mapped lesson preparation activity.
Any apparatus, microbiological culture or medical action is supervised or discussion-only unless teacher directs otherwise.
The 2023 learner-visible key remains an attempt-first self-check resource; hidden LMS assessments stay excluded.
Historical textbook statistics and medical/genetic claims require authoritative recheck before learner wording is finalized.
sourceAuditNotes: Printed textbook pages and PDF positions are enumerated individually; pages omitted from the supplied PDF cannot be inferred from a constant offset.
Chapter 11 workbook p. 22 question 14 is a blank branching immunity flowchart; question 15 has four lettered classifications.
Chapter 12 workbook p. 31 question 11 shows a three-generation pedigree with shaded people Sue, Joe, Jim and Tim. Question 11 has a–c subparts; question 13 asks learners to construct a pedigree.
Printed textbook p. 218 is cited by workbook pedigree question 11 but is absent from the supplied textbook PDF. Retain the workbook diagram and flag the missing page.
Guided notes are largely image-based. Page ranges are provisional until visual label and prompt checks are complete.
The 2023 workbook key is learner-visible only after an attempt; hidden Brightspace quiz/test banks are excluded.

Workbook p. 31 Q11 and p. 32 Q12 use different pedigrees. The 2023 key page 32 correctly identifies a recessive pattern for Q12 because its separate figure includes two unaffected parents with an affected child.
CBE supplemental page and image dispositions are in meta/cbe-content-audit-v2.md; no CBE image approved for direct learner publication.

scientificCorrections.sourceIssue: Older textbook/CBE descriptions limit vaccines to weakened or dead pathogens. CBE also frames vaccine-autism as a debate.
scientificCorrections.courseRule: Teach current vaccine platforms and immune memory; state clearly that MMR does not cause autism.

scientificCorrections.sourceIssue: Older workbook treatment prompts need current clinical wording.
scientificCorrections.courseRule: Antibiotics treat bacterial infections, not viral colds or flu; follow clinician/pharmacist directions, do not share.

scientificCorrections.sourceIssue: Workbook states XX/XY as a universal male/female rule.
scientificCorrections.courseRule: Use XX/XY as a common inheritance model, explicitly acknowledge variations and avoid inferring a person’s gender from a karyotype.

scientificCorrections.sourceIssue: Universal-donor language lacks component and clinical context.
scientificCorrections.courseRule: Qualify O-negative as the common emergency red-cell donor type; real transfusions require clinical compatibility checks.

scientificCorrections.sourceIssue: Q11 on p. 31 and Q12 on p. 32 use different pedigrees. Earlier course copy incorrectly applied the Q11 family relationships to Q12 and treated the key as flawed.
scientificCorrections.courseRule: Keep the figures separate. Use Q11 for generation, relationship and shaded-status reading. For Q12, explain that two unaffected parents with an affected child supports recessive inheritance in the intended simple model. Replace the source word 'infected' with affected trait status in authored instruction.
scientificCorrections.authority: Primary Unit C workbook and 2023 workbook key, pp. 31–32; supplied key-page image visually verified 2026-09-25.

scientificCorrections.sourceIssue: The workbook uses brown-dominant/blue-recessive human eye colour in Punnett and pedigree work.
scientificCorrections.courseRule: Label it explicitly as a simplified one-gene practice model, not a reliable prediction of a child’s actual eye colour.
